task.question: In an LCU-style assembly of a Hermitian piece, each selected term contributes a scaled controlled-phase source whose upper block carries the intended operator and whose lower-right filler block is normalizer times a phase e^{i*phi}. A source writes both filler phases as e^{i*pi} = -1 and claims the two filler blocks cancel so the clean block equals the intended Hermitian piece S1. Show by direct computation of the lower-right clean entry that the printed all-(-1)-phase choice does NOT cancel, give the exact value of that entry, prove the clean block therefore differs from S1 when the normalizer is nonzero, and exhibit the corrected phase assignment that does make the fillers cancel while preserving the intended operator blocks.
assumptions: Normalizer N (normalizerA) is a complex scalar; the counterexample needs N != 0
B is Hermitian (as in the PDE theorem) for the corrected block to equal S1
conventions: Each term scaled by 1/2; filler is N*e^{i*phi} on the lower-right diagonal
S1 is the Hermitian part of [[A,B],[0,0]] with lower-right block 0

cases.semantic_coverage: Whole-question matrix algebra: literal printed lower-right diagonal −N versus target zero, matrix inequality on an inhabited index set when N≠0, corrected zero filler and the unchanged three operator blocks, and corrected equality with S1 under Hermiticity of B. The phase choices and unitary implementation are not derived from arbitrary physical resource assumptions.
cases.shortcut_disclosure: The three named Eq. (29) result lemmas are available through the import. The library-assisted control combines them with a definitional preservation check. The constructed route computes the entry, uses that entry to refute equality, and compares the four corrected blocks. There is no single imported root theorem for the conjunction.

task.question: Let S and T be Hermitian matrices on one finite system and X a Hermitian matrix on a second system. Prove that H=S tensor X+T tensor I is Hermitian without assuming that S and T commute. Give a counterexample showing that the same conclusion can fail if X is not Hermitian.
assumptions: Finite-dimensional complex matrices; ordinary conjugate transpose
All declared products have compatible dimensions
conventions: Tensor factors ordered as written; stencil offsets are ordinary integers, not modular wrapping
Original derivation from inspected local source; no fresh Lean verification
